title: Esther
hook: When an ancient Persian king couldn't sleep, he did what any monarch might do—he asked for the court records to be read aloud, hoping the bureaucratic minutiae would lull him into slumber. Instead, that single sleepless night became the hinge on which an entire nation's survival turned. The book of Esther opens with the same Hebrew formula used throughout Scripture to mark pivotal moments—"And it was in the days of"—a phrase that signals we're entering not just a story, but a historical turning point where human choices and divine providence become indistinguishable. Here is a young Jewish woman who "puts on royalty" and walks uninvited into the king's presence, knowing she might die; a scheming official whose plot to destroy a people becomes the very mechanism of his own downfall; and a God whose name never appears in the text yet whose fingerprints are everywhere, working through insomnia, fasts, forgotten kindnesses, and one woman's breathtaking courage. In a world that often feels governed by chance and the whims of the powerful, Esther reveals how the turning points of history can rest on a single act of faith—and how sometimes the bravest thing we can do is put on our royalty and step forward when everything tells us to stay hidden.
